The discriminant and excluded singular boundary validate precise multiplicities. Included standalone exact polynomial and field checks agree.

originality.rationale: Explicit family is a known quotient model, but compared accessible primary literature and searched published mathematical records do not imply the exact exceptional polynomial sets, uniform p-rank-zero/four dichotomy, rank-two Cartier matrices at exceptions, or scheme multiplicities. Relevant stronger potential results and differing inertia types are addressed; residual unindexed historical priority risk is declared. Known characteristic-three special member C_{−1} is explicitly credited via the Kudo–Harashita–Senda supersingular example, so the assessed contribution is the complete marked stratification and determinant, not existence of this one curve.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed treatment of the C5 genus-four family could have derived equivalent explicit Cartier determinant and jumping divisors.

value.rationale: The motivating generalized-Fermat quotient model defines a natural order-five genus-four pencil. Its symmetry forces a nontrivial dichotomy of geometric p-ranks and permits full exceptional-locus and scheme-theoretic multiplicity classification in two small primes. Distinguishing a-number two from rank zero, and locating all double Hasse zeros, gives motivated arithmetic geometry not implied by generic ordinary assertions or mere method availability.
